graphInterpretation.title: Network Structure Interpretation

descriptions.hub: Central nodes with high degree act as critical risk transmission points in the supply chain network.
descriptions.downstream: Downstream entities inherit and accumulate upstream volatility through order amplification.
descriptions.tier: Risk is distributed across multiple tiers — upstream disruptions propagate downstream through inventory and order linkages.

graphInterpretation.hubPercentage: These {{count}} nodes account for {{percentage}}% of total network connections
graphInterpretation.isolatedRiskWarning: The following medium/high-risk nodes have very low connections (<5), possibly due to missing data or isolated risk points: {{nodes}}
graphInterpretation.pointCentralized: The network is centralized: Top 5 hub nodes concentrate {{percentage}}% of connections. These nodes are critical supply chain bottlenecks — prioritize ensuring their stability.
graphInterpretation.pointHighRiskLevel: All {{count}} high-risk nodes are at Level 1, the core operational layer. Risk is concentrated at the execution layer rather than the strategic layer.
graphInterpretation.pointCrossLevel: High-risk nodes emit {{count}} propagation edges to other tiers — risk may spread upstream/downstream through storage and plant relationships.
graphInterpretation.pointRemovedNodes: {{removed}}/{{total}} nodes in the raw data have no valid connections (insufficient degree) and were auto-filtered. Click "All Nodes" to view.
graphInterpretation.pointNodeSize: Larger node circle = more connections = more important in the network. Red = high risk, yellow = medium risk.
graphInterpretation.pointPriority: The priority table is sorted by "Importance = Connections × Risk Score" in descending order. Investigate nodes in this order.

tour.homeHero: Welcome to Saisca — offline supply chain risk analysis. In the next 60 seconds we walk you through a full demo.
tour.uploadDrop: Step 1: Import data. These are the 7 business tables of the built-in virtual case. Drag them into the area below. Data never leaves your machine.
tour.uploadNext: After dropping the files, click "Continue" to move on. No real upload happens.
tour.analyzeProgress: Six-stage analysis progress: structure, graph, risk, domain, decision, fingerprint. Every step is reproducible.
tour.resultSummary: Step 4: Results. Risk summary, high-risk nodes, and recommended actions — all from a traceable rule engine.
tour.resultDownload: Finally: export your report for sharing or archiving. Demo complete — thanks for watching!
tour.understand: Step 2: File understanding. Saisca identifies whether each table is nodes, facts, or relations, with row and column counts. Confirm and continue.
tour.mapping: Step 3: Field mapping. Every column mapping is shown transparently with status and confidence. No black box. Confirm and analyze.
tour.resultReasoning: Expand any high-risk node to see its full reasoning chain: data sources, computation steps, risk thresholds, triggers, and action basis — every step traceable.
tour.resultDomain: Domain insights: the engine auto-detects known supply chain patterns — bullwhip effect, VMI inventory, quick response — surfacing hidden fluctuation patterns.
tour.resultChartsTrend: Risk trend and distribution: how risk evolves over time and how it is spread across nodes, at a glance.
tour.resultNodes: Risk node table: risk scores and recommended actions for every node. "Try Change" lets you adjust parameters and compare decision impacts — but it needs the local analysis engine, so download the app to try it.
tour.resultGraph: Network topology: a 3D view of supply chain relationships. Lines show supply and delivery paths — drag to rotate.
tour.resultTimeline: Risk propagation timeline: how a failure at one node spreads through the chain, plus data confidence boundaries — what is reliable and what needs more data.
